rule_summary: The law names four kinds of foster family. General (almene) families care for children with light to moderate support needs, reinforced (forstærkede) families for moderate to severe needs, and specialised (specialiserede) families for severe needs. Network (netværks) foster families take a child they already know.
notes: Barnets lov, consolidated text LBK nr. 642 of 1 July 2026. Barnets lov has applied since 1 January 2024; the order on foster families made under it took effect the same day.

rule_summary: General, reinforced and specialised foster families must be approved by the socialtilsyn before they take a child for a placement or a support stay (støtteophold). A family can hold only one approval.
notes: The exception is an emergency placement under Barnets lov § 12, stk. 3. Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier, BEK nr. 1489 of 6 December 2023. borger.dk links to it as the order in force; we could not check on retsinformation.dk whether it has been amended since, as its pages are drawn by script.

rule_summary: Private foster care: nobody may take a child under 14 into private foster care for more than 3 months in a row without permission from the local municipal council. Permission is given only if a check finds the stay will benefit the child.
notes: This is an arrangement made by the person with parental responsibility, not a placement by the municipality. Barnets lov, consolidated text LBK nr. 642 of 1 July 2026.

rule_summary: No national cap on the number of foster children was found. Each approval states the number of places, along with the family's address and home, the type of foster family and what it offers.
notes: Lov om socialtilsyn, consolidated text LBK nr. 242 of 30 January 2026. Approved families are published on Tilbudsportalen, where municipalities search for them (Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden).

rule_summary: A network foster family is approved by the placing municipality as suitable for one particular child. The approval states its conditions, including the personal relationship it rests on. The decision cannot be appealed to another administrative body.
legal_citation: Barnets lov § 58, stk. 1 and 3; Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier § 10
notes: Barnets lov, consolidated text LBK nr. 642 of 1 July 2026. The family must normally be approved before the child moves in (Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier § 9, stk. 2).

rule_summary: Network foster families get no fee. The municipality covers board and lodging and the other costs of having the child. Up to DKK 20,000 a year per child can be paid as other costs without receipts. After an individual assessment they can also get full or part cover for lost earnings.
legal_citation: Barnets lov § 59, stk. 1; Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier §§ 14-17
notes: Lost earnings are paid as a taxable gross amount, with a pension contribution of 10 percent where the person had an employer pension (Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier §§ 15-17). A family can turn the payment down (Barnets lov § 59, stk. 2).

rule_summary: General, reinforced and specialised foster families must complete a basic course in being a foster family (grundkursus) as part of approval. Both foster parents take part. The course lasts at least 4 full days.
notes: The socialtilsyn must offer the course as part of approval (Lov om socialtilsyn § 5 a, stk. 2). Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier, BEK nr. 1489 of 6 December 2023. borger.dk links to it as the order in force; we could not check on retsinformation.dk whether it has been amended since, as its pages are drawn by script.

rule_summary: The basic course is two blocks of two days, held apart so applicants can reflect and talk with their own children. It covers caring for a foster child, child development and neglect, working with the child's network, and the legal framework.
notes: Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, BEK nr. 1559 of 5 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026. The course also gives the socialtilsyn information about the applicants.

rule_summary: Network foster families also take a basic course of at least 4 full days, with both parents. The placing municipality pays for it. If the child arrives first, the course must be done as soon as possible.
legal_citation: Barnets lov § 58, stk. 2; Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier § 11
notes: Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier, BEK nr. 1489 of 6 December 2023. borger.dk links to it as the order in force; we could not check on retsinformation.dk whether it has been amended since, as its pages are drawn by script.

rule_summary: The child's municipality must offer further training, supervision, advice and guidance that fit the task. Foster parents must take part. Further training is at least 2 full course days a year.
legal_citation: Barnets lov § 56, stk. 1; Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier §§ 5 and 12
notes: Specialised families must get extra training and supervision (§ 6). If several municipalities place children with one family, each covers its share of the 2 days. Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier, BEK nr. 1489 of 6 December 2023. borger.dk links to it as the order in force; we could not check on retsinformation.dk whether it has been amended since, as its pages are drawn by script.

rule_summary: Support is intensive in the first year of a placement: at least 1 extra course day, so at least 3 full days that year. It should normally start within the first half-year.
legal_citation: Barnets lov § 56, stk. 2; Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier §§ 7-8 and 13
notes: Municipalities use Social- og Boligstyrelsen's close start-up programme (tæt støttet opstartsforløb, TSOP) or one of the same scope. Foster parents must take part.

rule_summary: The socialtilsyn gets a child certificate (børneattest) and a criminal record certificate (straffeattest) for everyone in the household over 15. Each person consents through a request from the police in their digital post.
notes: Socialtilsyn Nord. Socialtilsyn Syd asks applicants to consent to a child certificate and a public criminal record certificate, and everyone over 15 at the address to a child certificate. Socialpædagogerne says 15 or over.

rule_summary: The socialtilsyn makes an overall assessment of whether the family's finances can support a stable placement. Applicants attach their latest tax statement, accounts if self-employed, and a monthly budget. Finances count equally with the quality model.
notes: Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden. Socialpædagogerne says the check is mainly of disposable income, not of how the family spends it. The socialtilsyn checks the family's finances every year after approval (Socialtilsyn Nord).

rule_summary: Every socialtilsyn follows one approval concept with three parts: the basic course, visits to the applicants' home using three tools, and a closing conversation. The tools look at mentalising resources, family dynamics and the views of children living at home.
legal_citation: Lov om socialtilsyn § 5 a; Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn § 5 and bilag 3
notes: In the mentalising interview, which is recorded, partners are interviewed separately and without children present. Socialtilsyn Syd says at least two home visits of about two hours, the first before the first course day. Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, BEK nr. 1559 of 5 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026.

rule_summary: The quality model has five themes and six criteria: the child's goals, the child's say and health, a safe and stable family, the foster parents' competences, and a home that supports the child. Each criterion is judged met or not met. To be approved, the family must be expected to meet them all.
legal_citation: Lov om socialtilsyn § 6; Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, bilag 2
notes: Socialtilsyn Nord says two earlier themes (education and employment; independence and relationships) and the scores from 1 to 5 were dropped on 1 January 2026. Some municipal pages still describe the older seven-theme model.

rule_summary: The law sets no room size. The home's surroundings, layout, facilities and condition must support the child's well-being, safety and right to privacy, and show that it is also the child's home.
notes: A socialtilsyn can approve on condition, for example that a room for the foster child is set up by a deadline (Socialpædagogerne). Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, BEK nr. 1559 of 5 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026.

rule_summary: Some municipalities ask for a furnished room for a full-time foster child.
notes: Næstved and Guldborgsund guidelines; Sønderborg asks full-time families for a room, bed and storage, and support families for a bed. Municipal practice, not a national rule.

rule_summary: No national rule on couples or single carers was found. Guldborgsund and Næstved say couples should have lived together for at least 3 years. Guldborgsund says single people can be approved for some tasks, such as support stays.
notes: Municipal guidelines. Copenhagen says some children need two parents and others do better with a single carer.

rule_summary: A couple living at the same address should normally both be on the application and both take part in approval. Both must attend every day of the basic course.
notes: Socialtilsyn Nord. The order says the course covers both foster parents where the family has more than one.

rule_summary: Some municipalities set a gap between the foster child and the family's own children. Næstved says own children should not be younger than 4; Guldborgsund says there should be at least 3 years between the foster child and children at home.
notes: Municipal guidelines, not a national rule.

rule_summary: The law sets no minimum age for foster carers. Socialpædagogerne says a socialtilsyn in the Capital Region approved a 21-year-old student.
notes: Socialpædagogerne is the trade union that organises foster carers. We found no age rule for foster carers in the order on foster families or the order on socialtilsyn.

rule_summary: No upper age limit for foster carers was found. Næstved says approval looks at the whole family, including the foster parents' relationship and ages.
notes: Næstved Kommune.

rule_summary: Applicants give information about their health. borger.dk has a self-service health declaration for foster families (Erklæring om helbredsforhold for plejefamilie).
notes: Næstved says applicants confirm in the declaration that their health lets them take on the task. The quality model looks at the family's health as part of its family structure (Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, bilag 2).

rule_summary: No separate smoking rule for foster homes was found. The quality model expects the family's care for the child's health to fit the child's age and needs, for example on diet, exercise, smoking, alcohol and drugs.
legal_citation: Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, bilag 2 (tema sundhed og trivsel)
notes: Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn, BEK nr. 1559 of 5 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026.

rule_summary: No particular education is needed to become a foster family. Background and experience can affect which type of foster family a family is approved as.
notes: Nordfyns Kommune; Vejle, Guldborgsund and Næstved say the same. Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden says specialised families often have solid experience or relevant training, though it is not required.

rule_summary: One foster parent may need to stay at home for a period, until the child is ready for nursery or school. Copenhagen says one parent often cuts hours or stops work for a while.
notes: Aalborg Kommune; Nordfyn and Viborg say the same. For specialised families an agreement to limit outside work fully or partly may be needed (Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden).

rule_summary: Socialtilsyn Syd asks applicants to attach a copy of their driving licence.
notes: No national rule on driving was found. Travel is agreed in the contract with the placing municipality (Copenhagen).

rule_summary: Foster carers are not employees. The family signs a contract with the placing municipality covering the fee, notice, travel and insurance. For tax, the fee counts as A-income, like wages.
notes: Familieplejen København; collective agreements for employees do not apply. Sønderborg says one foster parent signs the contract.

rule_summary: Socialtilsyn Syd says approval takes 12 weeks on average from when it receives the application.
notes: Copenhagen and Næstved say approval and the basic course can take up to half a year.

rule_summary: After an emergency placement with an unapproved family, the municipality can ask for fast-track approval. The socialtilsyn must then decide within 6 weeks of the placement decision.
notes: Conditions: the child is expected to stay beyond the emergency period, no approved family is available and network options have been explored. Lov om socialtilsyn, consolidated text LBK nr. 242 of 30 January 2026.

rule_summary: An approval has no end date. It lapses if a general, reinforced or specialised foster family has not been used for 3 years in a row, or if the family asks.
notes: For other services the period is 2 years. Lov om socialtilsyn, consolidated text LBK nr. 242 of 30 January 2026.

rule_summary: There is no renewal. The socialtilsyn visits each foster family at least every second year, usually unannounced, and checks its finances every year.
notes: From 1 January 2026 visits follow a shared risk model. Newly approved families, and families facing illness or divorce, may be visited more often (Socialtilsyn Nord).

rule_summary: The socialtilsyn can approve a family with conditions and a deadline; the approval lapses if they are not met in time. It can also allow a departure from an approval for a set period.
legal_citation: Lov om socialtilsyn § 5, stk. 7-8; Bekendtgørelse om socialtilsyn § 3, stk. 3
notes: Lov om socialtilsyn, consolidated text LBK nr. 242 of 30 January 2026.

rule_summary: The fee (vederlag) is taxable. It is set in the contract with the placing municipality as a number of standard units. KL's 2026 table sets one unit at DKK 5,244 a month (DKK 172 a day).
notes: KL (Local Government Denmark) publishes the table each year; the 2026 rates rose by 3.1 percent. Roskilde says a full-time foster family usually gets 5 to 8 units.

rule_summary: Board and lodging (kost og logi) is paid tax-free on top of the fee. In 2026 it is DKK 223 a day for a child under 10 and DKK 239 for a child aged 10 or over. For a third or fourth child from the same municipality it is DKK 206 a day.
notes: The law sets 200, 214 and 184 kr. a day at 2023 levels, adjusted each year (by 4.5 percent for 2026). KL also lists weekly rates for clothing and pocket money by age.

rule_summary: Under the average model (gennemsnitsmodellen), the fee is set once, at the start of a placement, for its whole length, with few exceptions. Roskilde uses it so foster carers need not fear a lower fee as the child makes progress.
notes: Vejle and Sønderborg also use it for full-time foster families; Copenhagen lets families choose it or the classic model. Search results show KL and Socialpædagogerne agreed in March 2026 to spread the model (unverified).

rule_summary: Families apply to the socialtilsyn for the region they live in. A socialtilsyn does not approve families in the municipality that runs it, so Frederiksberg goes to Syd, Holbæk to Hovedstaden, Faaborg-Midtfyn to Midt, Silkeborg to Nord and Hjørring to Øst.
notes: Familieplejen København lists the same split. Network foster families are approved by the placing municipality instead.

rule_summary: The basic course is free for applicants. No application fee for foster carers was found.
notes: Socialtilsyn Syd: free, with meals; travel is not paid. For network families the placing municipality pays (Bekendtgørelse om plejefamilier § 11, stk. 4).

rule_summary: No stated national rule was found. Copenhagen and Næstved say they value foster families of different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
notes: Familieplejen København; Familieplejen Næstved says the same.

rule_summary: An adoption can be granted only to a person aged 25 or over. Where there are special reasons, it can be granted from age 18.
notes: Adoptionsloven, consolidated text LBK nr. 669 of 1 July 2026.

rule_summary: When they apply, the applicant may not be more than 42 years older than the child. For a child aged 0 to 48 months, the application must be made before the applicant turns 43.
notes: Exceptions: a further child applied for within a reasonable time (Familieretshuset says 1½ years) after the first arrived, or special circumstances (§ 25, stk. 2). The rule does not apply to family or stepchild adoption (borger.dk). Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: Approval as an adopter lasts 4 years. It can be extended by 2 years, but only until the applicant is more than 47 years older than the child.
notes: A single adopter's approval lapses on marriage or after 2½ years of living with a partner (Familieretshuset). Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: Married and cohabiting couples adopt together. They must have lived together for at least 2½ years when they apply, or 1½ years if one is already approved. Single people can also be approved.
notes: Familieretshuset says this normally means a shared registered address for 2½ years. A single applicant is assessed on whether they can bring up a child alone, including their contact with family and friends.

rule_summary: Registered partners have had the same adoption rights as married couples since 1 July 2010. Cohabiting couples count whatever their gender.
notes: Familieretshuset. Being in fertility treatment or pregnant does not stop an application, but it is part of the final assessment.

rule_summary: The applicant's physical and mental health must not reduce the chance that the adoption is best for the child. The application includes a health certificate from the applicant's usual doctor, on an approved form and no more than 3 months old.
legal_citation: Bekendtgørelse om adoption § 8, stk. 3, and § 26, stk. 1, nr. 1
notes: The value is the most the certificate's age may be. Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: The applicant must have a home suitable for bringing up a child. There is no set size; location and layout can matter as much.
notes: Familieretshuset explains there are no objective size rules. Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: The applicant must have sound finances (forsvarlige økonomiske forhold), with room to support a family after the child arrives.
notes: Familieretshuset explains what sound finances means. Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: The applicant must not have convictions that give justified doubt about their suitability to adopt. Familieretshuset gets a full criminal record certificate.
legal_citation: Bekendtgørelse om adoption § 26, stk. 1, nr. 4, and stk. 2
notes: Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: First-time adopters must complete a pre-adoption course (adoptionsforberedende kursus) to be approved. It comes after phase 1 and is run by Ankestyrelsen. Couples attend together.
notes: Ankestyrelsen: four days in two residential parts about three weeks apart. Nothing said on the course is passed to Familieretshuset (§ 37). The Adoption Council can ask earlier adopters to attend again.

rule_summary: The pre-adoption course costs DKK 3,000, paid to Ankestyrelsen when signing up. It is not refunded after a cancellation less than 14 days before the start.
notes: Ankestyrelsen's page says DKK 3,000 per person. Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: Approval to adopt a child you do not know has four phases. Phase 1 checks age, relationship, health, criminal record, housing and finances. Phase 2 is the course. In phase 3 the Adoption Council (Adoptionssamrådet) decides on suitability after personal interviews. Phase 4 is counselling.
notes: Familieretshuset. Applications go in through its digital self-service (Bekendtgørelse om adoption § 8, stk. 2).

rule_summary: Adopters have 6 hours of compulsory adoption counselling, before and after the child comes home, with an adviser linked to Ankestyrelsen.
notes: Familieretshuset. Bekendtgørelse om adoption § 45, stk. 3, says adopters pay DKK 100 an hour for this counselling.

rule_summary: After a phase 1 decision to continue, the applicant must ask to start phase 3 within 3 months, or within 1 year if they must take the course first.
notes: The Adoption Council can make exceptions. Bekendtgørelse om adoption, BEK nr. 1755 of 30 December 2024, in force from 1 January 2025.

rule_summary: Applicants must have a fixed address in Denmark to apply for adoption under Danish rules.
notes: Familieretshuset.

rule_summary: A general approval covers a child aged 0 to 48 months with normal development potential. An extended approval is needed for an older child, siblings or a child with special needs. An approval can also be for one particular child.
notes: Familieretshuset. The value is the top age in months of the general approval.

rule_summary: No organisation now mediates new intercountry adoptions. DIA (Danish International Adoption) stopped on 16 January 2024, and people cannot join a waiting list for a child from abroad.
notes: borger.dk says Ankestyrelsen can finish cases begun before DIA closed. Adoption & Samfund says intercountry adoption is closed while it waits for political decisions.

rule_summary: The adoption grant is a tax-free one-off DKK 66,132 per child (2026). It is only for children adopted through DIA who have arrived in Denmark.
notes: Udbetaling Danmark handles applications, with a time limit of 6 weeks.

rule_summary: Family and stepchild adoption need no prior approval as an adopter. Some general rules, such as the 42-year age gap, do not apply.
notes: borger.dk. Familieretshuset handles these applications.

rule_summary: The Adoption Board (Adoptionsnævnet) matches children released for national adoption with approved adopters. It also hears appeals against refusals of approval.
notes: Ankestyrelsen runs the board's secretariat.
